reply.text:
Training can't fix that part, because the panic isn't a training problem, and I'd be dodging if I said otherwise. Lifting and running will do plenty for your strength, your energy and how you feel in your body. But if going over a number sets off real panic, that's worth talking through with a doctor or a dietitian who works with how people relate to food. That isn't a lecture, just the right person for it.

What I can do is keep the training side steady and make sure it never feels like something you have to earn food with. Want to tell me how the sessions have been feeling lately?
